canon.title: Florence and Rome, 1401–1564
canon.about: Classical facts of Florence and Rome from the competition for the Baptistery doors (1401) to Michelangelo's death (1564): art foremost, with its patrons, the politics of the Medici, the republic and the popes, and the letters and philosophy around them. A seed canon, drafted from general knowledge by a language model; every assertion names the standard reference it is to be checked against, and none is checked yet. Its selection is the canon of art history since Vasari: Florence first, famous men and their great commissions, the patrons as that history sees them; workshops, women, Venice and the rest of Italy are thin or absent, and where one of Vasari's or Condivi's anecdotes carries a sign the note says so. Dates are Julian, as the sources write them; a date that Florence wrote in its own style (the year beginning on 25 March) between January and 24 March is given in the modern year, and the note says so. Collective beings: the Signoria stands for the government of Florence through its successive regimes, the Medici for the family as a political house, the Calimala and the Opera del Duomo for the guild and the cathedral works that commissioned.

beings.name: Cosimo I de' Medici, Duke of Florence
The Medici, as a political house
The Arte di Calimala (the merchants' guild)
The Opera del Duomo of Florence

occasions.label: The Calimala's competition for the Baptistery's second doors: Ghiberti against Brunelleschi, each with a Sacrifice of Isaac
occasions.note: Ghiberti's Commentarii claim the palm outright; Manetti says the judges offered to share the commission and Brunelleschi refused. The panels were judged in 1402.

occasions.label: The Opera del Duomo's competition of models for the dome; Brunelleschi and Ghiberti among the competitors
Brunelleschi and Ghiberti appointed together to build the dome
occasions.note: With Battista d'Antonio; the dome was begun in August 1420. The month of the appointment is to be checked.

occasions.label: The Calimala commissions from Ghiberti the east doors, later the Gates of Paradise
occasions.note: 2 January 1424 in Florentine style; given here in the modern year.

occasions.label: Masaccio's Trinity in Santa Maria Novella, its painted architecture in Brunelleschi's manner
occasions.note: Brunelleschi's own part in the design is an attribution, not a document; Vasari says he taught Masaccio perspective.

occasions.label: Death of Masaccio in Rome, aged twenty-six
occasions.note: Vasari reports Brunelleschi's lament at the news.

occasions.label: Cosimo de' Medici arrested in the Palazzo della Signoria and exiled to Padua
Cosimo recalled from Venice; the Medici ascendancy begins
Alberti dedicates Della pittura to Brunelleschi, naming Donatello and Ghiberti beside him
occasions.note: The prologue also praises Luca della Robbia and Masaccio, then dead.

occasions.label: The competition for the lantern of the dome: Brunelleschi's model preferred to Ghiberti's and others'
Fra Angelico paints the altarpiece and the cells of San Marco, rebuilt at Cosimo's expense
Donatello's bronze David, made for the Medici
occasions.note: The date is disputed, from the 1430s to the 1460s; the statue stood in the Medici palace by 1469.

occasions.label: Death of Brunelleschi, buried in the cathedral by the Opera's leave
The Gates of Paradise set up at the Baptistery
Death of Fra Angelico in Rome
Cosimo gives Ficino a house at Careggi and Greek manuscripts of Plato to translate
Death of Cosimo de' Medici, Ficino reading Plato with him in his last days
occasions.note: Ficino's presence near the end rests on his own letter to Lorenzo.

occasions.label: Leonardo and Perugino in Verrocchio's workshop
occasions.note: Leonardo's apprenticeship is documented from the late 1460s; Perugino's there rests on Vasari. Giovanni Santi's rhymed chronicle (c. 1485) pairs them as two youths equal in age and in love.

occasions.label: Verrocchio's tomb of Piero and Giovanni de' Medici in San Lorenzo, for Lorenzo and Giuliano
Verrocchio's Baptism of Christ, an angel in it painted by Leonardo
occasions.note: Vasari's story that Verrocchio gave up painting on seeing the angel is not credited.

occasions.label: Lorenzo and Giuliano sell Verrocchio's bronze David to the Signoria
The Pazzi conspiracy: Giuliano killed and Lorenzo wounded at Mass in the cathedral; the Signoria hangs the conspirators; Sixtus IV stood behind the plot
occasions.note: Whether Sixtus IV consented to murder is contested: by Montesecco's confession he wanted the regime changed without bloodshed. War and interdict followed in June 1478.

occasions.label: Sixtus IV makes peace with Florence and absolves its envoys
Sixtus IV's contract with Botticelli, Ghirlandaio, Perugino and Cosimo Rosselli for the walls of the Sistine Chapel
Leonardo goes to Milan and offers Ludovico Sforza his services
occasions.note: The letter of offer survives in a copy; the Anonimo Gaddiano says Lorenzo sent him with a silver lyre. The year may be 1483.

occasions.label: Botticelli, Ghirlandaio and Perugino paint Lorenzo's villa at Spedaletto
occasions.note: Known from a Milanese agent's report on the painters of Florence (c. 1490), which names Filippino Lippi too; the frescoes are lost and their date is uncertain.

occasions.label: Ficino's Latin Plato printed, dedicated to Lorenzo; Pico arrives in Florence
occasions.note: That Pico arrived on the very day the Plato was published is Ficino's own story.

occasions.label: Death of Sixtus IV
Michelangelo apprenticed to Domenico and Davide Ghirlandaio for three years
occasions.note: Vasari prints the record from Ghirlandaio's book; Condivi passes over the apprenticeship. He stayed about a year.

occasions.label: Michelangelo, from the sculpture garden at San Marco, taken into Lorenzo's household
Savonarola returns to Florence, recalled with Lorenzo's consent at Pico's urging
Death of Lorenzo de' Medici at Careggi; Pico and Savonarola visit him
occasions.note: Poliziano's letter has Savonarola bless the dying man; a later Savonarolan life has him refuse absolution unless Lorenzo restored the city's liberty.

occasions.label: Death of Domenico Ghirlandaio
occasions.note: 11 January 1493 in Florentine style; given here in the modern year.

occasions.label: Piero de' Medici driven out; Savonarola, among the Signoria's envoys to Charles VIII, becomes the voice of the new republic
Death of Pico; Savonarola preaches at his burial in San Marco
Leonardo paints the Last Supper for Ludovico at Santa Maria delle Grazie
The bonfire of the vanities in the Piazza della Signoria
Alexander VI excommunicates Savonarola
Five citizens executed for plotting Piero de' Medici's return; Savonarola does not intervene for their appeal
The ordeal by fire fails; San Marco is stormed and Savonarola arrested by the Signoria
Savonarola hanged and burned in the Piazza della Signoria, papal commissioners present
Machiavelli elected Second Chancellor of the republic
Louis XII's army takes Milan; Ludovico flees, and Leonardo leaves the city
The Opera del Duomo and the Wool Guild commission the David
Cesare Borgia's patent names Leonardo his architect and general engineer
Machiavelli, Florence's envoy, at Cesare Borgia's court in Imola, where Leonardo draws his plan of the town
Cesare traps and kills his rebel captains at Senigallia; Machiavelli, with him, writes the account
Leonardo commissioned to paint the Battle of Anghiari in the hall of the Great Council
Machiavelli in Rome at the election of Julius II, who strips Cesare Borgia of the Romagna
Michelangelo taunts Leonardo in the street over the horse he never cast
occasions.note: An anecdote of the Anonimo Gaddiano, undated; placed here about 1504.

occasions.label: The committee on where to set the David: Leonardo, Botticelli and Perugino among its members
occasions.note: 25 January 1503 in Florentine style; given here in the modern year. Leonardo spoke for the Loggia dei Lanzi; the David went before the Palazzo della Signoria.

occasions.label: Leonardo's revised contract for the Anghiari, Machiavelli its witness
Michelangelo commissioned to paint the Battle of Cascina in the same hall as Leonardo's Anghiari
occasions.note: In the autumn of 1504; the month is approximate.

occasions.label: The David unveiled before the Palazzo della Signoria
occasions.note: Vasari's story of Soderini finding the nose too thick belongs here.

occasions.label: Julius II calls Michelangelo to Rome and commissions his tomb
Refused an audience, Michelangelo leaves Rome for Florence; the next day Julius lays the first stone of Bramante's St Peter's
occasions.note: Condivi blames Bramante's envy for turning the pope from the tomb.

occasions.label: Leonardo leaves for Milan on leave; Soderini protests that he has taken money and barely begun
Michelangelo, sent with Soderini's letters, submits to Julius II at Bologna and is given the pope's bronze statue to make
Michelangelo begins the Sistine ceiling for Julius II
occasions.note: Condivi says Bramante urged the commission in the hope that he would fail.

occasions.label: Raphael paints the Stanza della Segnatura for Julius II; Bramante portrayed in the School of Athens
occasions.note: Vasari says Bramante, his kinsman, brought Raphael to Rome and is the geometer of the School of Athens.

occasions.label: After the sack of Prato, Soderini deposed and exiled; the Medici return
Julius II says Vespers under the finished ceiling
Machiavelli dismissed from the chancery
Machiavelli, named in the Boscoli plot, imprisoned and tortured by the Medici regime
Death of Julius II
Giovanni de' Medici elected pope as Leo X; Machiavelli freed in the amnesty
Machiavelli tells Vettori he has written De principatibus, meant for a Medici
occasions.note: He hoped the Medici would employ him, even if they began by having him roll a stone.

occasions.label: Death of Bramante
Leo X names Raphael architect of St Peter's in Bramante's place
The Prince dedicated to Lorenzo di Piero de' Medici
occasions.note: The date of the dedication, and whether the book was ever presented, are uncertain.

occasions.label: Leonardo goes to France as Francis I's painter, lodged at Cloux
Cardinal Giulio de' Medici commissions Raphael's Transfiguration against Sebastiano's Raising of Lazarus, for which Michelangelo supplies drawings
Raphael's portrait of Leo X with Cardinals Giulio de' Medici and Luigi de' Rossi
occasions.note: Finished by September 1518, when it stood in for the pope at the wedding feast of Lorenzo di Piero de' Medici in Florence; the months are an estimate.

occasions.label: Michelangelo's contract with Leo X for the façade of San Lorenzo
Cardinal Giulio de' Medici commissions the New Sacristy of San Lorenzo, the Medici chapel
Death of Leonardo at Cloux
occasions.note: Vasari has him die in Francis I's arms; the court is documented elsewhere that week, and the story is not credited.

occasions.label: Leo X releases Michelangelo from the façade of San Lorenzo, to his bitter protest
Death of Raphael; the Transfiguration set at the head of his bier
Cardinal Giulio de' Medici, through the Studio, commissions Machiavelli's Florentine Histories
The imperial army sacks Rome; Clement VII besieged in Castel Sant'Angelo
occasions.note: The army was mutinous and unpaid; Charles did not order the sack.

occasions.label: The Medici expelled; the republic restored
Death of Machiavelli
The siege of Florence: the imperial army for Clement VII against the republic, Michelangelo in charge of its fortifications
occasions.note: Michelangelo was named governor of the fortifications on 6 April 1529, fled to Venice in September and returned in November. The siege ran from late October 1529; its end is the capitulation of August 1530. The coronation at Bologna fell within it, so the order of the two rests on the file.

occasions.label: Clement VII crowns Charles V emperor at Bologna
Florence capitulates; the Medici restored
Charles V makes Titian a Count Palatine and Knight of the Golden Spur
Michelangelo meets Clement VII; the Last Judgment probably first proposed
Death of Clement VII, two days after Michelangelo settles in Rome for good
The Last Judgment unveiled for Paul III
Titian in Rome at the Belvedere; Michelangelo and Vasari visit him, and Michelangelo praises his colour but regrets his drawing
Paul III makes Michelangelo architect of St Peter's
Titian at the imperial Diet paints Charles V at Mühlberg
Death of Paul III
Vasari's Lives printed by Torrentino, dedicated to Cosimo I, Michelangelo the one living artist in them; Michelangelo thanks him with a sonnet
Death of Charles V
Cosimo I in Rome, with Vasari, honours Michelangelo
The Accademia del Disegno founded at Vasari's urging, Cosimo I and Michelangelo its heads
occasions.note: 13 January 1562 in Florentine style; given here in the modern year. Michelangelo, in Rome, was elected in his absence.

occasions.label: Death of Michelangelo in Rome
occasions.note: 18 February 1563 in Florentine style; given here in the modern year. His body was taken secretly to Florence; the Academy's funeral in San Lorenzo (July 1564) and Vasari's second edition (1568), which ends with his Life, lie beyond this canon.

ties.note: Both claimed the dome; the joint appointment of 1420 is left unsigned.
The Signoria is the government of each regime: under the Medici it acts with them, under the republics against them.
The deathbed blessing is Poliziano's account; the Savonarolan legend of a refused absolution would sign it -1.
A friar's obedience to the pope, coded as service: open defiance is -1.
The admiration of the dispatches, and later of The Prince, ch. 7.
In 1529 the commission is the republic's fortifications, architecture by an artist in its pay.
After the siege Clement pardoned him and had him finish the Medici chapel (1530).
He presented the Florentine Histories to Clement VII in Rome in May 1525.
Reconciled by the Treaty of Barcelona, 29 June 1529.
Mixed: praise to Titian's face, regret for his drawing to Vasari after; the occasion is remembered for the regret (codebook §6).
Michelangelo declined Cosimo's repeated invitations to return to Florence.
